text: Early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene came to the tomb and saw that the stone had been taken away from the tomb.

versions.text: Early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene came to the tomb and saw that the stone had been taken away from the entrance.
versions.explanation: The Greek reads "taken away from the tomb" (ἐκ τοῦ μνημείου). "From the entrance" adds a detail not in the text; keeping "from the tomb" is accurate and reads just as smoothly.

text: So she ran to Simon Peter and the other disciple, the one Jesus loved, and told them, "They have taken the Lord out of the tomb, and we don't know where they have put him."
So Peter and the other disciple set out for the tomb.
They were both running, but the other disciple outran Peter and reached the tomb first.
He bent down and looked in, and saw the linen cloths lying there, but he did not go in.
Then Simon Peter came up behind him and went into the tomb. He saw the linen cloths lying there,
and the cloth that had been around Jesus' head was not with them but folded up by itself in a place of its own.
Then the other disciple, who had reached the tomb first, also went in. He saw, and he believed.
For they still did not understand the Scripture, that he had to rise from the dead.
Then the disciples went back home.
But Mary stood outside the tomb, weeping. As she wept, she bent down to look inside,
and she saw two angels in white sitting there, one at the head and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain.

versions.text: and she saw two angels in white sitting where the body of Jesus had lain, one at the head and one at the feet.
versions.explanation: The reordering leaves the phrase "one at the head and one at the feet" dangling after the main clause, which is awkward when read aloud. Following the Greek order keeps the picture clear and builds to the poignant final phrase.

text: "Woman, why are you weeping?" they asked her. "They have taken away my Lord," she said, "and I don't know where they have put him."
With that she turned around and saw Jesus standing there, but she did not know it was Jesus.

"Woman, why are you weeping?" Jesus said to her. "Who is it you are looking for?" Thinking he was the gardener, she said, "Sir, if you have carried him off, tell me where you have put him, and I will take him away."
Jesus said to her, "Mary." She turned to him and said in Aramaic, "Rabboni!"—which means Teacher.
Jesus said to her, "Do not hold on to me, for I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go to my brothers and tell them, 'I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.'"
Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, "I have seen the Lord!" And she told them that he had said these things to her.

versions.text: Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, "I have seen the Lord!"—and that he had said these things to her.
versions.explanation: The dash joining a direct quotation to an indirect clause is hard to render in oral reading. Breaking it into a second sentence preserves both parts of the Greek without the grammatical mismatch.

text: That evening, on the first day of the week, the disciples were together behind locked doors for fear of the Jewish leaders. Jesus came and stood among them and said, "Peace be with you."

versions.text: That evening, on the first day of the week, the disciples were together behind locked doors for fear of the Jews. Jesus came and stood among them and said, "Peace be with you."
versions.explanation: In this Gospel οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι often designates the hostile authorities in Jerusalem rather than the Jewish people as a whole (the disciples themselves were Jews). Rendering it "the Jewish leaders," optionally with a footnote noting the literal "the Jews," avoids an unintended blanket implication.

text: After saying this, he showed them his hands and his side. The disciples were overjoyed when they saw the Lord.
Again Jesus said to them, "Peace be with you. As the Father has sent me, so I am sending you."
And with that he breathed on them and said, "Receive the Holy Spirit.
If you forgive anyone's sins, they are forgiven; if you withhold forgiveness, it is withheld."
Now Thomas, one of the Twelve, called the Twin, was not with them when Jesus came.

So the other disciples told him, "We have seen the Lord!" But he said to them, "Unless I see the mark of the nails in his hands and put my finger where the nails were, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe."
Eight days later his disciples were together again indoors, and Thomas was with them. Though the doors were locked, Jesus came and stood among them and said, "Peace be with you."
Then he said to Thomas, "Put your finger here; look at my hands. Reach out your hand and put it into my side. Stop doubting and believe."
Thomas answered him, "My Lord and my God!"
Jesus said to him, "Have you believed because you have seen me? Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed."

versions.text: Jesus said to him, "You have believed because you have seen me. Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed."
versions.explanation: The Greek is punctuated as a question, and the interrogative form sets up the contrast with the beatitude that follows. Rendering it as a flat statement loses the gentle challenge in Jesus' words.

text: Jesus did many other signs in the presence of his disciples that are not recorded in this book.
But these are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in his name.
